unsupported_inference: That a hit/contact condition caused the apparent early teardown. The probe recorded none of the proposed gate inputs, branch outcomes, or hit/contact events, so temporal adjacency to a shared destructor cannot establish that causal link.
preserved_observations: Instance A was created with lifetime 32, observed at update checks with lifetimes 32 and 31, and then followed immediately in sequence by a shared-destructor event returning to 0x216f9cc.
Instance B was created with lifetime 30, observed at update checks with lifetimes 30 and 29, and then followed immediately in sequence by a shared-destructor event with the same return address.
Other kind-0x00 instances counted down and had teardown signals near lifetime zero.
The observations establish a repeated two-update-check pattern followed by an adjacent shared-destructor signal, not confirmed per-element destruction or elapsed frame count.
missing_evidence: Direct attribution of each destructor event to the corresponding ObjShot element.
The value of elem+0x26 bit 0x80, the tested 0x4/0x8 values, or the resulting contact-gate branch outcome for those elements.
Any recorded collision, contact, hit, damage, or knockback event preceding teardown.
next_instrumentation: At the teardown-triggering branch or call site, log the ObjShot element pointer and the evaluated hit/contact-gate result; this is the smallest observation that can both attribute teardown to the instance and test the proposed cause.
